pr.title: Converge generator checks and fix metadata self-tests and KaTeX
pr.body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

Terraform's generator, exact-path verifier and artifact gate used separate implementations from the accepted PowerShell foundation. This PR ports the common implementation from [PS234](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/234), accepted at `98177628b7bc02c646724bfc8aa0fd73fed0cd24`. Terraform retains its language descriptors, independent output allowlist and actual recovery semantic checks.

The generator prepares complete payloads before publication and uses the shared versioned result contracts. The artifact gate retains bounded child execution, checked native status, the first resolved Node executable and final identity checks. The build requires 156 generator assertions twice on each of Windows PowerShell 5.1, Windows PowerShell 7 and native-ext4 Linux PowerShell 7 for the same revision before artifact publication.

Two hosted runs exposed a metadata fixture defect at UTC midnight: synthetic documents kept the previous day's date while child validators read the new day. Private fixture clock controls now cover the actual current, delayed, accepted-worktree, proposed, local and capacity callers. They check exact source anchors and completed clock readbacks, preserve primary errors and remove their state after each action. The production validator and its date policy retain accepted bytes.

Further testing found that literal brackets in a checker path were interpreted as a wildcard by `Set-PSBreakpoint`. The helper now applies `WildcardPattern.Escape` only to its two breakpoint path arguments. Source reading and execution retain the original literal path. The persistent regression uses `clock-probe[fixture].ps1` and the matching decoy `clock-probef.ps1`; it requires exactly two new breakpoints, both on the intended file. Existing negative clock controls and cleanup assertions remain in place.

A fresh audit also identified [GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7) in the Markdown checker dependency graph. An exact workflow-root override selects KaTeX 0.18.2 under `micromark-extension-math@3.1.0`. This crosses the parent's declared range; installation and lint compatibility were checked explicitly. Current callers parse math syntax, and no browser rendering exploit was established here. The dependency-maintenance note records why the override is needed and when to remove it.

## Scope and decisions

The PR changes 16 files: the original 12-file generator port, the SelfTest, two workflow package files and the dependency-maintenance note. The common generator and artifact logic retain only the exact Terraform descriptors and `TerraformRecovery` semantics. CI helpers and build retain repository identity, Terraform's existing `verify` role and output scope. The script index retains the Terraform semantic entry and T1 provenance reference. The four generated documents retain their accepted bytes.

The midnight repair selected C97 after comparing eight options, with correctness across callers and preservation of the production validator weighted highest. The dependency repair selected the exact parent-version override at 96.5/100 after comparing twelve options. The literal-path repair selected B97.5 after comparing ten options: documented escaping preserves the exact checker identity and existing clock controls with a meaningful decoy regression. Scores are engineering judgments; the executed controls provide behavioral evidence.

Round2's Windows-runner concern was refuted by GitHub's supported runner labels and the successful exact-head Windows jobs. The command-length concern was also refuted by measured Windows/Linux limits and actual helper/caller round trips. All three review threads received one disposition and are resolved. The separate literal-path defect is repaired here. Supporting records: [runner decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/ca5488aa5d48cc187d657a325d322843973300a4/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A03/TF68-R3-windows-runner.md), [transport decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/ca5488aa5d48cc187d657a325d322843973300a4/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A21/TF68-R4/DECISION.md), [literal-path decision](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/58aab1903eeb19d3f18fc32ab7359ecde9f45dd5/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A21/TF68-R5/DECISION.md).

Round3's output-type finding is fixed: `ConvertFrom-NulPathRecordStream` now declares `[OutputType([byte[]])]`, matching each emitted byte-array record. Only that annotation and the file/function NOTES versions changed from the previous reviewed candidate. The function body and public behavior remain unchanged. The decision selected B100 after comparing seven options. Supporting record: [precise output type](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/46f952b8fb25fcf1427d899b0938e0d724e67f42/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A06/TF68-round3/R8-output-type.md).

The other three distinct Round3 suggestions received validated no-change decisions: the private unknown-artifact guard retains its fixed diagnostic because the current public catch does not expose the proposed detail; Node resolution retains the first Application and its actual launch error because a file-existence check neither validates a shim nor removes a race; Windows acquisition/proof code retains the currently matching inline implementation under the existing admission policy. These are current-input decisions, with future triggers stated in their records: [diagnostic](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/46f952b8fb25fcf1427d899b0938e0d724e67f42/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A06/TF68-round3/R6-unknown-artifact.md), [Node path](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/46f952b8fb25fcf1427d899b0938e0d724e67f42/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A06/TF68-round3/R7-node-path.md), [workflow duplication](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/46f952b8fb25fcf1427d899b0938e0d724e67f42/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A06/TF68-round3/R9-workflow-duplication.md). All four decisions used separate weighted rubrics before implementation. Scores express engineering judgment, not measured certainty.

## Validation

The current local candidate is `3b12700eb636da67f5861637e5b139a18fa82140`, tree `a4e7ce67d14cb4d5b4e0b677ff995ff4adbd2d29`, against accepted Terraform base `e21b74fe0b56551008f78f9f2946cd2a0f9c19ce`.

- The final R8 candidate passed all four affected Linux artifact-wrapper cases and all 11 mandatory repository hooks, with zero failures or skips. The staged preflight and final source/dependency/Git guards passed. The other 78 tracked files and 1,914 dependency files retained their frozen bytes.
- The actual final function AST reports exactly System.Byte[]. Probes verified zero, one and multiple output records, preservation of raw newline/UTF-8/0xFF bytes, and zero partial output from three malformed streams. The original metadata fails the precise contract as expected. PowerShell 7.6.5 and PSScriptAnalyzer 1.24.0 report zero parser/analyzer issues. These probes were not added as implementation-mirroring product tests.
- Normal commit hooks and all five actual accepted-base/current-head checks passed: maintenance classification, accepted content, whole-PR author finalization, metadata classification and proposed policy. The ordinary two-root audit is CLEAN with no findings or risk exceptions. Independent bounded decision and implementation review found no material issue.
- Validated unchanged-input evidence remains attributed to the prior `7dd48f5` candidate: all 567 Node tests with zero failures/cancellations/skips; generator 156 assertions twice, unchanged generated outputs and independent Terraform semantics; R5 path matrices (10 Windows and 14 Linux cases), clock controls, actual callers, cleanup and transport limits. R2 retains 244 affected tests per platform and checked Windows installs. The small R8 metadata delta received the affected tests above; no separate full local 567-test rerun is claimed for it.
- The prior `7dd48f5` candidate passed all 11 ordinary hosted runs, including both 567-test behavior runs, both 11-hook setup runs and both three-platform generator/artifact runs. Round3 Copilot's agentic setup was cancelled at its 20-minute limit; an actual Lite review delivered six comments. The cancellation is preserved as such and is not called a passing workflow. Remote Codex completed with no findings on that prior input.

Fresh current-input remote reviews, hosted checks and final native binding remain required before merge. No failing-CI merge is permitted; any CI relaunch is limited to once per hour for this PR. Local Linux does not replace hosted ext4 proof. No new local Windows PowerShell 5.1 execution or recovery-harness acceptance is claimed. The initial R8 local launch failed before tests because Docker was stopped; one ordinary service start allowed the unchanged qualified image and manifest to run.

After normal reviewed landing and actual landed-workflow verification, carry the common SelfTest, script-index metadata, dependency files/note, and artifact-helper annotation/metadata back to current PowerShell main. This is a six-path prospective repair, subject to the actual accepted commit comparison. Compare raw bytes again and retain only justified differences. This PR does not complete the paired plan, recovery harness or human approval gates. Existing filesystem limitations remain tracked in [PS155](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/issues/155).

What changed in this PR This PR ports the shared PowerShell generator/artifact-gate foundation from the accepted PSStyleGuide PR234 into TerraformStyleGuide, keeping Terraform's own language descriptors and state-recovery checks. asserts 4 verify steps and platform-role mutation categories. | | `.github/​workflows/​workflow-policy-cases.json` | Shifts verify step indices (0→1…3→4) and adds platform/admission mutation cases. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-StyleGuideArtifacts.ps1` | Adds `Assert-ChildIntegrity`, two semantic-role branches, and `StyleGuide.GeneratorResult.v2` schema check. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-StyleGuideGenerator.ps1` | New harness exercising generation/publication/identity controls with host + ext4 validation. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-ExactGitPathSet.ps1` | Renames schema to `StyleGuide.ExactGitPathSetResult.v2` and bumps versions. | | `.github/​workflows/​Test-CiHelpers.test.mjs` | Adds generator-proof/admission/acquisition and PowerShellExamples role tests. | | `.github/​workflows/​Classify-InstructionMaintenance.mjs` /​ `.test.mjs` | Registers `Test-StyleGuideGenerator.ps1` as a recognized selector. | | `.github/​workflows/​scripts-README.md` | Adds the harness row to the script index. | | `.github/​workflows/​Generate-StyleGuideArtifacts.ps1` | Emits the renamed `StyleGuide.GeneratorResult.v2` schema consumed by the gate (per PR description). |

Embedding the full text of `Invoke-AgentInstructionFixtureClock` into a `pwsh -Command` string risks hitting OS/process command-line length limits (and makes failures harder to debug when quoting/escaping changes). A more robust approach is to write the helper function to a temporary `.ps1` file (or reuse an existing fixture helper file) and dot-source it in the child process, then invoke `Invoke-AgentInstructionFixtureClock` normally.
